title: Yakisugi House / Estudio Mazara
text:
Yakisugi House / Estudio Mazara

Designed by Mazara Estudio Arquitectura, this private residence establishes a close dialogue between its built spaces and the surrounding tropical landscape. The architectural composition brings together elongated horizontal volumes, lightweight pitched roofs, and a restrained material palette of natural stone, wood, and dark-toned structural elements.

title: MIAA - Iberian Museum of Archaeology and Art / Carrilho da Graça Arquitectos
text:
MIAA - Iberian Museum of Archaeology and Art / Carrilho da Graça Arquitectos

The city of Abrantes is, materially and historically, a landmark within a broader territory—an expression of the geostrategic opportunity found on a promontory at the geometric center of a region defined by geopolitical conventions, while simultaneously marking the transition between two landscape units of distinct morphologies. Standing watch over the landscapes on which it rose, Abrantes developed as both an eye and a beacon, a fortified outpost and an obligatory crossing point, in times of peace or war. Atop a telluric, foundational topos, human occupation established its opportunity to dwell, creating its locus, both systemically and inextricably linked.

title: A Geometric Ruin / 00L
text:
A Geometric Ruin / 00L

Inhabiting the open landscape of the Córdoba hinterland calls for an act of spatial delimitation and the establishment of a domestic order. Located in La Bolsa, this low-cost residential project adopts the patio as the generative principle of its architectural layout, drawing on a dwelling type deeply rooted in the history of architecture. Its references include Jørn Utzon's celebrated Kingo Houses and Alvar Aalto's Muuratsalo Experimental House, both of which explore the L-shaped house organized around an open space, establishing an articulated relationship between domestic intimacy, landscape, and collective life.

title: MAS House / SUITE
text:
MAS House / SUITE

Located in São Paulo, Casa MAS is the result of a complete renovation designed with spatial integration as its starting point and materiality as its structuring element. Developed by SUITE, the residence was redesigned to respond more precisely to the family's dynamics, promoting fluidity, comfort, and a consistent connection between indoors and outdoors.

title: Goldring Woldenberg Riverfront Park  / Eskew+Dumez+Ripple
text:
Goldring Woldenberg Riverfront Park / Eskew+Dumez+Ripple

For decades, the riverfront at Goldring Woldenberg Riverfront Park was a hard industrial edge: sheds, trucks, and security fencing separating residents and visitors from the Mississippi. After Hurricane Katrina, the Reinventing the Crescent plan reframed the waterfront as a tool for recovery, resilience, and long-term economic development, envisioning more than six miles of continuous public space along the river.

title: Dust Egypt's Forgotten Architecture, Revised and Expanded Edition
text:
Dust Egypt's Forgotten Architecture, Revised and Expanded Edition

Between 1860 and 1940, Cairo and other large cities in Egypt witnessed a major construction boom that gave birth to extraordinary palaces and lavish buildings. These incorporated a mix of architectural styles, such as Beaux-Arts and Art Deco, with local design influences and materials. Today, many lie empty and neglected, rapidly succumbing to time, a real-estate frenzy, and an ongoing population crisis.

title: Unearthing the Ground: Architecture and the Politics of Water
text:
Unearthing the Ground: Architecture and the Politics of Water

When the Ostrogoths besieged Rome in 537 AD, their first military act was to cut the aqueducts. Eleven gravity-fed channels supplied the city with up to a million cubic meters of water per day, more than enough to sustain a population of over a million, fill the public baths, and scour the sewers. Without the aqueducts, Rome became a fortified enclosure around a contaminated river, proving that water was essential to the city's existence.

title: Recycling Park / Bovenbouw
text:
Recycling Park / Bovenbouw

In 2009, the City of Antwerp launched a competition to rethink municipal waste infrastructure — a typology typically relegated to generic asphalt lots and containers. Bovenbouw won with a master plan treating the recycling park not as an industrial backlog, but as essential, high-frequency public space. Following early siblings like the recycling centres Luchtbal and Borgerhout, Kielsbroek is the lineage's last addition, aiming to highlight the destigmatization of waste management.

title: Kengo Kuma & Associates’ Water Culture House to Open in Copenhagen on December 5, 2026
text:
Kengo Kuma & Associates’ Water Culture House to Open in Copenhagen on December 5, 2026

Designed by Kengo Kuma & Associates in collaboration with Cornelius Vöge Atelier for Architecture and Vilhelm Lauritzen Architects, KAI Water Culture House is set to open on December 5, 2026, on Papirøen (Paper Island) in Copenhagen, Denmark. The 5,800 m² public facility combines ten indoor and outdoor pools, wellness facilities, cultural spaces, and access to Copenhagen Harbour. Comprising five brick towers above a glazed base, the project brings together swimming, recreation, and cultural programming as part of the ongoing transformation of the city's waterfront.

title: AD—WO to Renovate the Heinz Architectural Center at Pittsburgh’s Carnegie Museum of Art
text:
AD—WO to Renovate the Heinz Architectural Center at Pittsburgh’s Carnegie Museum of Art

Pittsburgh's Carnegie Museum of Art has commissioned architecture and urban design practice AD—WO to reimagine the Heinz Architectural Center. The practice, led by Emanuel Admassu and Jen Wood and one of the winners of the ArchDaily 2026 Next Practices Awards, was recognized for exploring relationships among people, place, history and material culture, bringing an interdisciplinary approach to the architecture experience. The Heinz Architectural Center is the museum's forum to present, explore and incubate architectural ideas, currently located in the institution's main building, which dates from 1907. The new design aims to transform the Center into a contemporary facility that brings together exhibitions, collections, research, learning and public engagement. AD—WO is working with R3A as architect of record, Buro Happold for engineering and sustainability, Tillotson Design Associates for lighting and VizzAcoustics for acoustics.

title: Obra Blanca 2026 Explores the Connection Between Materials and Design
text:
Obra Blanca 2026 Explores the Connection Between Materials and Design

Direct contact with a material allows one to appreciate textures, compare finishes, and observe how its appearance changes under different lighting conditions. At an exhibition, these possibilities are complemented by exchanges with manufacturers and professionals, helping to understand applications and resolve questions about their use. This relationship between material exploration and architectural practice was one of the central pillars of the seventh edition of Obra Blanca, which drew more than 23,000 professionals to Expo Santa Fe in Mexico City.

title: Inhabiting as Inquiry: Threads from the 20th Buenos Aires International Architecture Biennial
text:
Inhabiting as Inquiry: Threads from the 20th Buenos Aires International Architecture Biennial

Inhabiting a space involves multiple economic, social, cultural, geographic, political, and environmental factors. Beyond these considerations, however, it engages with processes, boundaries, and possibilities that have repeatedly become subjects of architectural inquiry. "We are builders of a society," declared Solano Benitez during his lecture titled The Place of Architecture at the Buenos Aires International Architecture Biennial. Through a series of international lectures, exhibitions across different locations in the city, and activities open to all generations, the 20th Buenos Aires International Architecture Biennial examined the value of inhabitation, recognizing architecture as the discipline that gives meaning to how and where we live and, consequently, how we exist within society.

title: House between Gardens / Studio BHD
text:
House between Gardens / Studio BHD

Set within Val de Vie Estate in the Paarl Winelands, House Between Gardens is conceived as a contemporary family home shaped by landscape, climate and the rhythms of everyday living. The architecture reinterprets the Cape vernacular H-plan to create a series of interconnected internal and external spaces, allowing the house to sit not simply alongside its landscape, but between and within a collection of gardens.

title: Nazuna Hakone Miyanoshita Hotel / STUDIO ALUC
text:
Nazuna Hakone Miyanoshita Hotel / STUDIO ALUC

Nazuna Hakone Miyanoshita is a newly opened ryokan in Hakone by Nazuna, a brand originally established in Kyoto. We were responsible for the design of its refurbishment. While Nazuna has traditionally reinterpreted Kyoto culture through the contemporary re-editing of wooden machiya townhouses, this project required the expression of Kyoto-like qualities within the constraints of a reinforced concrete (RC) structure in Hakone.

title: UMG sede Antigua Guatemala / Atelier oficina de Arquitectura
text:
UMG sede Antigua Guatemala / Atelier oficina de Arquitectura

The UMG Campus in Antigua Guatemala represents a critical case study in bridging traditional colonial architecture with massive institutional scale. Developed by ATELIER Oficina de Arquitectura, the primary challenge of this project was adapting a small-scale colonial design to a large-scale complex. We understood early in the planning phase that simply replicating historical facades is insufficient without considering the context and the diverse needs of a student complex.

Haras Larissa Residence / Ricardo Gusmão Arquitetos

title: Casa Cibeles / Taller Síntesis + 23 constructora
text:
Casa Cibeles / Taller Síntesis + 23 constructora

Casa Cibeles is located in the municipality of La Ceja, a region characterized by open landscapes, gentle topography, and a strong presence of native vegetation. This natural setting not only frames the project but also defines its starting point: conceiving a home that respects the site, minimizes its footprint, and allows the landscape to maintain its continuity.

title: Claranet Portugal Headquarters / PROMONTORIO
text:
Claranet Portugal Headquarters / PROMONTORIO

Claranet is an IT company providing network hosting and managed application services (Hybrid Cloud Hosting) to corporate clients across Europe and Brazil. The practice was invited to design its Portuguese headquarters on the site of a former military depot, itself built on the grounds of the 17th-century Grilas Sisters' convent. The convent survived the 1755 earthquake but not the 1834 extinction of the religious orders. It became state property and in 1897, was converted into military warehouses. After the 2016 Web Summit, the city rescued it to create Lisbon's International Innovation Hub, now a group of municipal concession buildings for tech-based services and creative industries.

text:
CS3 - Event & Sports Pavilion / HA+MA

CS3 is an Event and Sports Pavilion situated in Los Angeles, CA. Constructed of mass timber, the structure offers a variety of spaces and facilities for sports, outdoor activities, social events and food service.
